newsitem.title: UK: BA accuses TGWU of leading members to strike.
newsitem.headline: BA accuses TGWU of leading members to strike.

text.p: British Airways Plc accused the Transport and General Workers' Union of leading its members towards what it called an unnecessary conflict with the airline.
The union gave its backing to BA cabin crew strike on Tuesday after those balloted had voted overwhelmingly in favour of action last week over a five-month-long pay dispute.
BA said its chief executive Bob Ayling had written to TGWU general secretary Bill Morris to suggest opening talks on the cabin crew dispute with the assistance of an independent arbitrator.
"I have had conversations with Bill Morris, with the sole intention of breaking the deadlock between us," Ayling said in a statement. "
"I had been led to believe that we were on our way to achieving just that on the ground issue and yet the union seems intent on strike action."
TGWU couldn't immediately be reached for comment.
Ayling said BA will continue to work on a local basis to resolve the problems. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
